ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier, Articles L561-1 through L561-34 and R561-1 et seq.; Article L561-2-2 (definition of beneficial owner and 25% ownership threshold); Articles L561-45 et seq. (TRACFIN obligations); Décret n° 2016-1601 du 25 novembre 2016 on the beneficial-owner register; Directive (EU) 2018/843 (AMLD5) transposed by French law; and Regulation (EU) 2015/849 as amended.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National notary or competent public authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (HCCH 1961 member) or Consular Legalization by the French Consulate in the document's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registrar of the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization by the French Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of address for each UBO and manager (utility bill or original bank statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature certificate and, where required, Hague Apostille or French Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Judicial record extract or criminal background certificate for each manager and UBO

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, managers, and counterparties against: (i) the European Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (EU restrictive measures), (ii) UN Security Council sanctions resolutions, (iii) OFAC SDN List, and (iv) French domestic asset-freezing measures. PEP screening is required under Articles L561-10 and R561-18-2 of the French Monetary and Financial Code, using a risk-based approach. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for UBOs connected to non-EEA jurisdictions identified by FATF or the French Finance Ministry as high-risk. Screening results and rationale must be documented in the pre-incorporation file and updated at least semi-annually for enduring SARL relationships.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique électronique (formalities.entreprises.gouv.fr) and Infogreffe – Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) portal (www.infogreffe.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be freely available, written in French or in a Latin-script transliteration, and must not infringe public order or pre-existing distinctive rights. Foreign-script names require a certified Latin transliteration; Arabic, Cyrillic, Chinese, or other non-Latin characters are not accepted as the official corporate name without a transliteration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCS or the Guichet unique refuses registration on grounds of name unavailability or a prohibited token, the applicant must, within 30 days of the refusal, submit an administrative appeal addressed to the president of the competent commercial court (juge délégué à la surveillance du registre du commerce) attaching the original refusal notification, copies of all incorporation documents, and a revised name proposal; the court decides within 15 days; no further charge applies if rectification is accepted and re-submitted through the Guichet unique.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only through a licensed commercial domiciliation company in accordance with Article L123-11-2 of the French Commercial Code. For a cleanroom modular interior fit-out SARL, a virtual office alone is insufficient: a verifiable operational site or bonded warehouse will be required to support trade licences, professional insurance, and contractual performance; a letterbox arrangement without commercial substance is rejected in French tax and AML practice.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 25% during the first two fiscal years for a construction-sector SARL, with unannounced site-level labour and URSSAF inspections being more frequent than head-office inspections.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.210-1 to L.210-10, L.223-1 to L.223-43, R.210-1, R.223-1; Code civil Article 1832; Décret n°2007-431 of 25 March 2007 on the Register of Commerce and Companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) administered by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce de Paris, with filings centralized through the INPI Guichet Unique des formalités des entreprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic application form M0 filed through the Single Window, accompanied by the certified Articles of Association (Statuts) and mandatory annexes, including capital deposit attestation and legal notice certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital applies to a SARL (Code de commerce, L.223-2); the capital is freely fixed in the Articles of Association. At incorporation, cash contributions must be fully subscribed, and at least one-fifth of the cash capital must be released and deposited on a blocked account with a bank or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations. Contributions in kind are fully paid in at incorporation and require approval by the partners or a contribution auditor if applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: By these resolutions, the subscribing partners: (1) adopt the Articles of Association and approve subscription and contribution of shares in a total nominal value as set forth in Exhibit A, acknowledged fully subscribed; (2) fix the registered office at 128 Rue de la Chaussée d'Antin, 75009 Paris, France; (3) appoint [Name Surname] as Manager (Gérant) of the Company with full powers to represent the Company for its corporate purpose, including opening bank accounts, signing contracts and undertaking health, safety and environmental obligations; (4) authorize the Manager to complete all registration formalities with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce and the competent administrative authorities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute French SARL Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Partners or a licensed notaire in France; the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce de Paris through the Guichet Unique accepts the signed Articles for registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Statuts in French in accordance with Code de commerce Articles L.223-1 and R.223-1. Ensure the company name, form, registered office, corporate object, share capital, duration, manager details and allocation of shares are clearly stated. Each subscriber must sign the Articles. If any contribution in kind exceeds EUR 30,000, include a report from a registered contribution auditor (commissaire aux apports). For real estate contributions, execute the Statuts as a notarial deed. Prepare the corporate purpose centred on cleanroom modular interior fit-out, including HVAC engineering, cleanroom wall partitions, suspended ceilings, raised floors, containment fabric, and related installation, testing and maintenance services.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or national ID of each partner
Lease agreement or title deed for the proposed registered office
Draft and final signed Articles of Association
Detailed list of contributions in kind with valuation reports or auditor report if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or Greffe identifies conflicting clauses, execute a rectification deed in the form prescribed by R.210-4 and submit it before the registration application; if the corporate object is considered unlawful, amend the Articles by a general meeting of partners.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit Paid-up Capital on a Blocked Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French commercial bank or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open an account in the name 'SARL [Company Name] en formation'. Pay the cash contributions as required by the Articles; at least one-fifth of the full subscribed cash capital must be deposited, with the balance payable within five years. The depositary issues the attestation de dépôt de capital, to be attached to the registration file. Verify that the beneficial owner declaration aligns with the deposit amounts and the identity of each contributor.
required_dossiers: Cash contribution remittance statements for each partner
Partner identification and tax residence declarations
Signed copy of the subscription share list
Draft Articles of Association for the bank or notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the depositary raises an identity or source-of-funds query, supply the requested bank references and documentary evidence; if the capital remains blocked more than ten days, coordinate with the bank to maintain the attestation until the RCS registration is completed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish a Legal Notice of Company Formation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) authorized in the department of the registered office, Paris.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select a JAL authorized to publish for the department of Paris (75). Submit the draft notice containing the company name, SARL legal form, share capital amount, registered office address, corporate purpose, duration and the date of the Articles. The notice must appear prior to or simultaneously with the RCS application. Obtain the attestation de parution and preserve it for the registration file. The publication certificate remains valid for one year.
required_dossiers: Identified company name and trademark similarity research report
Full corporate purpose text from the Articles of Association
Registered office address proof
Legal notice draft provided by the JAL
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL requires additional disclosures regarding corporate purpose or legal form, revise the notice and republish; if publication is delayed, obtain a dated duplicate certificate and file it as soon as issued, with an explanatory cover note to the Greffe.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the Registration Application with the Single Window
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); competent Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce de Paris.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the M0 electronic form through the national Single Window. Attach the executed Articles of Association, capital deposit certificate, legal publication certificate, identity documents, declaration of beneficial owners and, if applicable, power of attorney. The Guichet Unique routes the file to the Greffe, which verifies legality of the Articles and statutory compliance. Pay the official registration fees through the portal. Natural-person managers must provide their national identity card and proof of address.
required_dossiers: M0 form completed with all company and manager fields
Signed Articles of Association, certified if notarial deed
Bank attestation de dépôt des fonds
Legal publication certificate (attestation de parution)
Declaration of beneficial owners (DBE)
Power of attorney if a third party submits the file
Lease or proof of right to use the registered office
Identity documents of managers and partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe queries the application, remedy within fifteen days by adding the missing annexes through the Single Window. In case of invalid Article clauses, execute a rectification deed and attach it. If the company name conflicts with a prior registration, select a new distinctive name, amend the Articles and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Kbis Extract and Complete Fiscal and Social Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce de Paris, INSEE, Direction générale des Finances publiques, URSSAF.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After validation of the RCS application, retrieve the Kbis extract, which certifies company existence and legal status. INSEE assigns SIREN, SIRET and APE/NAF code, and the data is automatically transmitted to the tax and social security administrations. Open a professional operational bank account. Register as an employer with URSSAF or the CARSAT, create electronic payroll declaration access, and retain the company registration for insurance coverage, including décennale and civil liability policies.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract issued after registration
Bank account opening form and company corporate documents
Employer registration forms with URSSAF
Workplace health and safety registration declaration with Santé au Travail
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis extract is delayed, request an interim certificate from the Greffe. If URSSAF or tax administration notifications are missing, present the Kbis and register directly online. If the APE code is inaccurate, file a modification request with INSEE.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: DRIEETS Île-de-France for occupational safety and workplace licensing; DREAL Île-de-France for environmental and ICPE permits; Préfecture de Police de Paris for fire safety and civil defense clearance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'exploitation d'installation classée pour la protection de l'environnement (ICPE) under registration/déclaration regime for the modular cleanroom manufacturing workshop; plus site-specific 'Plan Particulier de Sécurité et de Protection de la Santé (PPSPS)' for each fit-out project.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: DREAL Île-de-France (Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: ICPE Enregistrement or Déclaration under Rubrique 2940 for surface treatment and solvent storage; a full environmental impact assessment is mandatory only when the activity exceeds the thresholds of Article R.122-2 of the French Environmental Code or is located in a sensitive or Natura 2000 zone.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges: pH 6.5-8.5, COD ≤125 mg/L, suspended solids ≤35 mg/L, no net addition of listed hazardous substances; air emissions: total volatile organic compounds (VOCs) ≤40 mgC/m3, particulate matter ≤10 mg/m3; solvent-containing wastes, paints and adhesives must be traced through the Bordereau de Suivi des Déchets (BSD) and treated by licensed operators.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification by the SDIS 75 or a certified building control agency for the workshop and cleanroom systems; structural load inspection and certification for partition wall systems, suspended ceilings and HVAC equipment support; occupational health clearance by the Service de Prévention et de Santé au Travail confirming compliance with the Labour Code on ventilation, lighting, noise, electrical safety, machine guarding, first aid and emergency response.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – principal tax authority for corporate taxation and VAT; online portal www.impots.gouv.fr. Foreign direct indirect tax registration is processed by the Service des Impôts des Entreprises Étrangères (SIEE) in Paris.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Non-resident SARLs must obtain a French tax identification number (TIN) and a VAT number by filing Form Cerfa n° 16431 with the Service des Impôts des Entreprises Étrangères (SIEE) before carrying out taxable operations in France. The application must be accompanied by proof of legal existence (certificate of incorporation from the foreign registry, articles of association), a copy of the foreign VAT registration certificate, and power of attorney for the appointed tax representative. The SIEE normally issues the French SIRET/SIREN number within 2–4 weeks, after which a French intra-Community VAT number is assigned and registered on the EU VAT Information Exchange System (VIES).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not apply the US check-the-box system. SARLs are generally subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés). Under Article 239 bis A of the French General Tax Code, a small SARL may elect to be taxed as a pass-through partnership (régime des sociétés de personnes) for up to five years if the legal form qualifies and the election is filed with the DGFiP. Additionally, French tax consolidation (intégration fiscale) is available to companies controlling 95%-owned EU subsidiaries. With respect to indirect taxes, no hybrid mismatch election exists for VAT, but a taxpayer may request a specific ruling (rescrit fiscal) to confirm the VAT treatment of cross-border transactions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée – TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For non-resident suppliers making taxable supplies in France, there is no de minimis VAT registration threshold: any B2B service or good supplied to a French customer requires registration. For existing French-established small businesses, the annual turnover thresholds for the VAT exemption (franchise en base de TVA) are €85,000 for sales of goods and €34,400 for provision of services; exceeding these thresholds triggers mandatory registration. The 2025 thresholds may be adjusted for inflation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing compulsory electronic invoicing and e-reporting for all established taxpayers. From 1 September 2026, all taxable persons must be able to receive electronic invoices, and large enterprises must issue them; from 1 September 2027, the requirement extends to all enterprises. Invoices must comply with a structured format (Factur-X, UBL 2.1, or CII 16.1) and be transmitted through the mandatory public access portal (Portail Public de Facturation, PPF) or a certified partner platform (Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire, PDP) connected via API. There is no digital stamping duty for standard intra-EU/export invoicing, but customs import/export declarations are made electronically via the DELTA/CDU system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods shipped outside the European Union are zero-rated (0% VAT) under Article 262 CGI provided the supplier meets the proof-of-export requirements. For intra-EU supplies to a VAT-registered customer, the supplier may apply the exemption (0% rating) for intra-Community supply under Article 262-2 CGI. For services (including cleanroom fit-out services supplied to a non-EU client), the place of supply is considered outside France under Article 259A CGI (B2B rule), making the service either out of scope or zero-rated if the recipient is a taxable person established outside the EU, subject to supporting documentation. Eligibility is denied if the service is physically rendered in France for a French recipient.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAE – Déclaration d'échange de biens / export summary declaration via DELTA)
Bill of Lading, CMR consignment note, or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank credit note) proving receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency
Commercial invoice with incoterms and reference to the export exemption
Proof of exportation within the time limit (normally 12 months from supply)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The French tax administration scrutinises export zero-rating claims by cross-checking customs export data (DX7/DXG). Failure to produce the required export documentation within the statutory period results in reversal of the zero-rate, recovery of VAT at 20%, plus late interest (intérêt de retard) at approximately 0.20% per month and manipulation penalties of 80% of the tax due in cases of deliberate non-compliance. Criminal fines up to €75,000 and imprisonment are possible for tax fraud (fraude fiscale). A retrospective clawback can be assessed up to the normal tax limitation period (usually three years).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), the national central bank of the French Republic within the Eurosystem of the European Central Bank (ECB), is the principal monetary, payment-systems, and balance-of-payments surveillance authority. Exchange control competence is exercised jointly with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) under the Code monétaire et financier (in particular Articles L.151-1 et seq. on financial relations with foreign countries), while the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) licenses and supervises credit institutions, payment institutions, and electronic-money institutions for banking, FX, and AML/CFT compliance. The euro is the legal tender and the sole domestic currency; no separate national exchange control agency issues foreign-exchange licenses in France.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France operates under the principle of fully liberalized and convertible capital and current accounts. Article L.151-1 of the Code monétaire et financier declares that financial relations with foreign countries are free, without prejudice to international sanctions, prudential regulations, and anti-money-laundering statutes. The euro is fully convertible for current-account flows (trade, services, dividends, interest, royalties, salaries) and capital-account flows (equity subscriptions, shareholder loans, repatriation of liquidation proceeds, portfolio investment) in accordance with Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the Eurosystem's foreign-reserve policy. No exchange-control authorization, license, or convertibility certificate is required for profit remittances by an SARL; the practical hurdles are domestic corporate and tax gateways rather than FX controls: the SARL must have legally distributable profits approved by the shareholders within the statutory period following the financial year-end, the statutory balance sheet must not trigger the prohibition on distribution where net assets would fall below capital, and non-resident shareholders must apply applicable tax treaty relief or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive in order to reduce the default domestic dividend withholding tax. All non-resident settlements are subject to threshold-based statistical reporting discharged by the French order bank on behalf of the Banque de France.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement, no mandatory repatriation timeline, and no compulsory conversion ratio. The pre-1990 obligation to repatriate and surrender export revenues to the national foreign-exchange system was abolished as part of the full liberalization of French exchange controls and is incompatible with the euro-area legal framework. A French SARL may lawfully retain export receivables in any convertible currency in either domestic or foreign bank accounts, may disburse them directly in the same currency for imported inputs, subcontracting, or hedging settlements, and is merely obliged to translate and revalue foreign-currency positions at each statutory reporting date under French accounting standards. Practical constraints are limited to (i) the threshold-based reporting of cross-border payment transactions with non-residents, discharged by the order bank for the Banque de France; (ii) the obligation to maintain normal commercial documentation (invoices, delivery proofs, customs declarations) evidencing the underlying export transaction; and (iii) the anti-money-laundering requirement that any large or unusual receipt be traceable to a genuine trade transaction.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. and LCL (Crédit Lyonnais)
BPCE — Banque Populaire and Caisse d'Épargne / Natixis (Corporate and Investment Banking)
Crédit Mutuel Alliance Fédérale and CIC

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: HIGH for European Economic Area electronic-money institutions (EMIs) that hold an ACPR e-money license in France or benefit from an EU/EEA payment-institution or EMI passport into France under the Revised Payment Services Directive (PSD2), provided they offer euro and multi-currency accounts, SWIFT and SEPA outbound rails, and expense cards. Representative French or passporting players can serve the SARL for day-to-day working-capital management and cross-border treasury reconciliation. Feasibility rating: LOW for offshore digital EMIs lacking a French or EEA license: such entities cannot lawfully provide payment services in France, cannot open a French IBAN-based collection account, have no standing under the French deposit-guarantee framework, and their safeguarding arrangements would not be supervised by the ACPR. Legal constraints: an EMI may not grant credit, issue documentary letters of credit, or issue bank guarantees, so the cleanroom-fit-out contracting SARL must retain a licensed credit institution as its primary banking and trade-finance provider; an EMI's client funds must be held in segregated safeguarding accounts, and the EMI must apply the same KYC/AML standards required by the French Monetary and Financial Code.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a French SARL, at least one gérant (or another statutorily authorized representative) must complete the KYC interview; the interview may be conducted via secure videoconference with electronic identity verification for directors holding a valid French or EEA identity document and a French residence address, in line with ACPR-endorsed remote onboarding practices and eIDAS-level electronic signatures. For non-resident or foreign-national gérants, French banks in practice require physical attendance at an appointed branch of the account-opening jurisdiction, unless the bank accepts a written power of attorney granted before a French notary or a foreign consulate, apostilled under the Hague Convention, translated into French by a sworn translator, and accompanied by the certified K-bis extract of the company; in such cases a remote interview of the authorized representative and of the ultimate beneficial owner is still required. When opening the capital escrow account for the SARL en formation, the gérant must additionally sign the bank's formation-account mandate and, later, the release instruction supported by the certificate of incorporation; the bank verifies the actual receipt of the subscribed capital and issues the statutory certificate of deposit (attestation de dépôt des fonds) required for the RCS registration process.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) opacity — non-resident shareholders, foreign intermediate holding vehicles, or trust-like structures without clear identification of the final natural persons.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified French UBO declaration form; complete ownership organigramme from the SARL up to each final beneficial owner; certified copies of identity documents; three-to-six-month personal bank statements of each UBO evidencing source of wealth; constitutional documents and share register of the SARL and, for each intermediate entity, the relevant registry extract or audited accounts; where a trust or foundation is present, a legal-opinion letter summarizing the settlor, protector, and beneficiary structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ambiguity in the source and purpose of funds for the initial capital injection and for shareholder loans, creating a risk that the flow is recharacterized as an unsubstantiated treasury advance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Minutes of the shareholders' meeting resolving the capital increase or approving the shareholder loan; written shareholders' loan agreements (conventions de trésorerie) with commercial interest terms and repayment schedule; bank statements of the lending shareholders evidencing the source and path of funds; the bank's blocked-account certificate (attestation de blocage des fonds / certificat de dépôt des fonds); and the gérant's sworn statement on the genuineness of the subscribed capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Failure to evidence the statutory license, professional qualification, and insurance required for the cleanroom HVAC and interior fit-out contracting activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: K-bis extract of the SARL issued within the previous three months showing the registered commercial activity; trade-registry registration documents and, where applicable, the professional qualification certificates for cleanroom installation, HVAC works, and interior fit-out (for example QUALIBAT, OPQIBI, or equivalent sector certifications); certificate of professional indemnity insurance and mandatory ten-year building liability insurance (assurance décennale); URSSAF registration and social declarations; and the company's health-and-safety risk assessment document (Document Unique d'Évaluation des Risques) where employment is present.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, politically exposed person (PEP), or adverse-media flags on the SARL, its shareholders, or its key commercial counterparties, particularly where customers or suppliers are located in jurisdictions subject to EU, UN, or foreign restrictive measures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Screening reports from a commercial sanctions and PEP database with a documented audit trail; detailed explanation and structure chart for any flagged counterparty; independent French or international legal opinion on applicable sanctions and export-control exposure; and full contractual file showing the genuine commercial project (tender, contract, bill of quantities, advance invoices) with confirmation that no restricted party is involved.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (balance sheet, profit and loss account, annex) and management report approved by the ordinary general assembly, followed by RCS deposit of the certified accounts.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce (Registre du commerce et des sociétés – RCS) in the company’s registered-office departement.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ordinary general assembly must approve the annual accounts within six months of fiscal year-end; the approved accounts must be filed with the commercial registry within one month after approval. For a fiscal year ending 31 December the indicative deadlines are 30 June and 31 July respectively.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to deposit accounts can lead to a judicial injunction with daily astreinte, criminal liability for the manager, and persistent default may trigger judicial dissolution or administrative strike-off (radiation) of the SARL.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Form 2065-SD with the 2050-series annexes) including the tax balance sheet, income statement, and related schedules.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction generale des Finances publiques (DGFiP) – Service des impots des entreprises.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year fiscal period the return is due electronically by 3 May of the following year; for a non-calendar year-end it is due no later than the second business day after 1 May following the close of the fiscal year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late submission triggers a 10% late-filing penalty, increased to 40% after formal notice, plus late-payment interest of 0.2% per month; failure to file may also lead to tax assessment ex officio and penalties up to 80% for deliberate concealment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local business contribution – Cotisation Fonciere des Entreprises (CFE): updated information declaration and final annual payment of the local economic foot tax.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction generale des Finances publiques (DGFiP) – Service des impots des entreprises.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The annual CFE information return is filed by the second business day following 1 May; final payment of the current-year CFE is due 15 December, with 15 June and 15 December instalments where the annual CFE exceeds EUR 3,000.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing and payment attract automatic penalty increases (10% if paid within 30 days of the deadline, 40% after formal notice) plus late-payment interest of 0.2% per month; under-declaration of chargeable property may also cause retroactive assessment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A SARL must appoint a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) when, for two consecutive financial years, it exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds: total balance sheet above EUR 4,000,000; net revenue excluding tax above EUR 8,000,000; average workforce above 50 employees. A statutory auditor is also required in certain group scenarios or upon a court-approved request by shareholders holding at least one-tenth of the capital.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual statutory accounts must be prepared under French GAAP (ANC Regulation 2014-03, Plan comptable general). IFRS as adopted by the EU may be used only for consolidated financial statements and is not available for the statutory individual accounts of a standalone SARL.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: French law does not impose a separate annual UBO renewal filing. The beneficial-owner declaration (DBE) is filed initially at RCS registration and must be updated whenever a share transfer or other event modifies beneficial ownership; the updated declaration is filed with the commercial registry within 30 days of the change. At the annual closing, the manager must reconcile the Register of Members with share-transfer documentation and the Minute Book; if no triggering event has occurred, no duplicate annual UBO filing is required.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members and share-transfer state (registre des associes)
Register of Directors / corporate officers (registre des mandataires sociaux)
Minute Book of shareholders’ and directors’ decisions
Register of Beneficial Owners (registre des beneficiaires effectifs)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$300–US$1,500 per year for a registered-office or corporate agent domiciliation service in France; a full annual secretarial compliance service including accounts deposit and register maintenance is typically US$1,000–US$3,500.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$4,500–US$25,000 per year for a certified statutory audit of an SARL in the cleanroom modular fit-out construction sector, depending on revenue, balance-sheet size, number of project contracts, and consolidation requirements.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% corporate income tax, generally applicable to taxable profits of a French SARL.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: A qualifying small enterprise may apply a 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to applicable turnover, capital ownership, and fully paid-up capital conditions; the standard 25% rate applies above that amount. Qualifying innovation, research, investment, and regional incentives may reduce the effective rate but are fact-specific. French tax credits generally reduce tax payable rather than taxable income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: No fixed five-year expiry. Tax losses may generally be carried forward indefinitely, subject to an annual utilization cap of EUR 1 million plus 50% of the portion of current-year taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. Carryback is generally available for the immediately preceding financial year, capped at the lower of that year's profit and EUR 1 million, subject to formal election.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD, corporate income tax return, filed electronically through the French Tax Administration professional portal (impots.gouv.fr, espace professionnel) using EFI or through an approved EDI accounting or tax provider. Supporting corporate tax schedules generally include Forms 2058-A-SD through 2058-C-SD and Forms 2059-A-SD through 2059-G-SD.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with corporate income tax instalments generally payable quarterly or on the statutory French instalment schedule.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a financial year ending on a date other than 31 December, the return is generally due within three months after the financial year-end. For a 31 December year-end, the electronic return is generally due on the second business day following 1 May of the following year. The applicable annual administrative calendar must be checked for the precise filing date. Corporate income tax instalments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December, subject to statutory exceptions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, SIREN number, registered office, tax office, financial year opening and closing dates, and applicable corporate tax regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder is not reported as the taxpayer unless it operates through a French permanent establishment or French taxable entity. Report the French SARL as the taxpayer and identify foreign shareholders in the ownership and related-party information where required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit or loss after reconciling statutory accounting profit with French tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only income and deductions attributable to the French SARL. A foreign parent’s income, expenses, and losses must not be imported unless legally attributable under an arm's-length transaction or permanent-establishment allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs and deductions reconciling accounting income to taxable income, including non-deductible expenses, provisions, depreciation adjustments, exempt income, and tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Test cross-border management fees, royalties, interest, guarantees, and recharges for deductibility, arm's-length pricing, withholding tax, beneficial ownership, and business-purpose requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year tax loss, carried-forward losses utilized, remaining losses, and any elected carryback amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the French annual loss-utilization cap. A foreign group loss or foreign tax loss cannot be deducted merely because the shareholder or parent incurred it.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax treatment of disposals of fixed assets, shares, and other capital assets, including relevant holding-period and participation-exemption calculations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Analyze French-source rules and applicable tax treaties for gains realized by foreign shareholders on a disposal of SARL interests; do not assume a French taxing right without treaty and domestic-law review.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 2059-B-SD, allocation of capital gains and losses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Classification and allocation of taxable and exempt capital gains and losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Separate ordinary operating gains from gains subject to special participation or long-term regimes and retain acquisition, valuation, and ownership evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax depreciation, exceptional depreciation, and adjustments for assets used in the French fit-out, construction, HVAC, cleanroom, and modular partition activities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Document asset ownership, commissioning dates, useful lives, work-in-progress, subcontractor capitalization, and allocation between French and foreign operations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-recognized provisions and impairment charges, including recoverability and reversal information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Customer, contract, warranty, and inventory provisions must be supported by identifiable risks and sufficiently reliable estimates; generalized group provisions are vulnerable to disallowance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Turnover, value-added, and information used for tax and statistical analysis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile turnover with VAT returns, statutory accounts, project progress certificates, retention amounts, and intra-group invoices.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, foreign tax credits where available, instalments, withholding amounts, and balance payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign taxes are creditable only under French law or an applicable treaty and must be supported by official evidence. Do not offset foreign withholding against French corporate tax without confirming the relevant limitation and documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Required information regarding certain executive compensation and benefits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include compensation paid directly or indirectly by foreign group entities where French disclosure rules capture the arrangement and retain payroll, board, and recharge documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information concerning subsidiaries, participations, shareholdings, and related corporate relationships.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose foreign parent, subsidiaries, controlled entities, and material participation interests accurately and reconcile the disclosures with statutory accounts and transfer-pricing records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: French transfer-pricing declaration, documentation, and, where applicable, country-by-country reporting or notification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report cross-border controlled transactions, identify counterparties and jurisdictions, and maintain Local File, Master File, and CbC materials where statutory thresholds apply.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing may trigger a 10% penalty, increased in specified circumstances to 40% or 80%, together with late-payment interest generally calculated at 0.20% per month. Failure to file after formal notice can lead to automatic assessment, increased penalties, loss of procedural protections, and separate penalties for inaccurate or incomplete information. Tax fraud may create criminal exposure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2572-SD for corporate income tax balance, Form 2571-SD for corporate income tax instalments where applicable, and electronic payment through the impots.gouv.fr professional portal or authorized EDI channel.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual balance settlement with periodic instalments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The balance is generally payable by the statutory deadline for the final corporate income tax payment following the relevant financial year-end. Instalments are generally due on the statutory quarterly dates, subject to exemptions, minimum-tax rules, and applicable administrative calendars.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax liability after deduction of instalments, credits, and permitted withholding offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use only tax legally attributable to the French SARL and reconcile the amount to Form 2065-SD and the general ledger.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax instalments paid, tax credits, and other permitted prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign parent payments are not French tax instalments unless made on behalf of the French SARL and properly recorded and evidenced.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Bank account, payment amount, payment date, and electronic tax payment reference.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain proof of payment and ensure the paying bank account is authorized for the French entity; payment by a foreign group company does not change the SARL's liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment generally attracts 0.20% monthly late-payment interest and may result in a 5% payment penalty in addition to filing-related penalties. Repeated non-payment may trigger formal collection, liens, account seizures, director liability in exceptional cases, and criminal proceedings for fraudulent insolvency or tax fraud.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: French VAT returns, generally Form CA3 (3310-CA3-SD), filed electronically through the impots.gouv.fr professional portal or EDI; the applicable regime may require monthly, quarterly, or annual reporting.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Monthly or quarterly under the normal regime; annual summary or payment arrangements may apply under simplified regimes, subject to turnover and tax thresholds.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return is generally due during the following month by the date assigned to the taxpayer in the professional tax account. Construction and fit-out businesses must separately analyze domestic reverse-charge rules for qualifying subcontracting and cross-border supplies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Domestic taxable sales, reduced-rate transactions where applicable, exports, intra-EU supplies, and services supplied to business customers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Classify each project by place-of-supply rules, customer status, installation location, export evidence, and whether the transaction is a supply of goods, service, or immovable-property-related work.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Input VAT on materials, equipment, subcontractors, rentals, professional services, and operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain compliant invoices, customs evidence, import VAT records, and business-purpose support. Foreign VAT is generally recovered through refund procedures rather than deducted on the French VAT return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: VAT due by the recipient under domestic or cross-border reverse-charge rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Review subcontracting, imported services, intra-EU acquisitions, and imported goods separately; incorrect reverse-charge treatment can create both VAT and penalty exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: CA3, net VAT payable or credit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Output VAT less deductible input VAT, VAT credits, and payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile to sales ledgers, project certificates, customer invoices, customs declarations, and bank receipts.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or payment generally triggers a 5% penalty and 0.20% monthly late-payment interest; omitted or understated VAT can attract 40% or 80% penalties depending on intent and conduct. Fraudulent VAT arrangements may result in criminal prosecution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: The domestic French withholding tax rate on dividends and similar distributions paid to a non-resident is generally 25%, subject to treaty relief, statutory exemptions, and anti-abuse rules. A qualifying EU or EEA parent may obtain an exemption under the French implementation of the Parent-Subsidiary Directive, generally requiring qualifying ownership, minimum holding conditions, and anti-abuse compliance. Dividends paid by a French SARL to a French-resident corporate shareholder are generally not subject to dividend withholding tax, although the participation exemption and 5% share of costs and expenses must be analyzed.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Confirm the recipient's tax residence, beneficial ownership, treaty eligibility, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose requirements, holding percentage, holding period, and applicable treaty article before payment. Obtain the recipient's current certificate of tax residence and complete the relevant French Forms 5000 and, where applicable, Forms 5001 for dividends, 5002 for interest, or 5003 for royalties. Provide documentation to the French payer or paying intermediary before payment whenever possible; otherwise apply for a refund within the prescribed period. Maintain ownership charts, board approvals, payment records, treaty forms, and evidence that the recipient is not a conduit. Treaty relief cannot be claimed solely because the recipient is incorporated in a treaty jurisdiction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French domestic withholding on royalties and similar payments to non-residents is generally 25%, subject to treaty reductions or exemptions and special rules for payments to non-cooperative or blacklisted jurisdictions. Ordinary interest paid by a French company to a non-resident is generally not subject to French withholding tax under domestic law, except for specified anti-abuse, non-cooperative-jurisdiction, or instrument-specific situations; treaty provisions must nevertheless be checked. Treaty rates commonly range from 0% to 15% for interest and from 0% to 15% for royalties, but the exact rate depends on the applicable treaty, beneficial ownership, source characterization, and anti-abuse conditions. Interest deductibility is separately limited by French thin-capitalization, earnings-stripping, anti-hybrid, and related-party rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full French Local File and Master File documentation is generally mandatory where the French entity or French tax group has annual pre-tax turnover or gross assets of at least EUR 400 million, or belongs to a group meeting the EUR 400 million threshold. Documentation may also be required in a tax audit for entities below the threshold, and material cross-border related-party transactions must be supportable regardless of threshold. The French simplified transfer-pricing declaration, generally Form 2257-SD, may apply to entities meeting the statutory conditions, including relevant turnover or gross-asset thresholds and controlled transactions. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to qualifying multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no standalone regime titled Economic Substance Regulations equivalent to certain offshore ESR regimes. Nevertheless, substance is material under French transfer-pricing rules, beneficial-ownership analysis, anti-abuse provisions, permanent-establishment principles, controlled foreign company rules, anti-hybrid rules, interest limitation rules, treaty principal-purpose tests, and the general abuse-of-law doctrine. A French SARL should maintain genuine French management, decision-making, personnel or appropriately controlled operational capacity, premises where commercially appropriate, accounting records, bank activity, project execution evidence, and functions consistent with its remuneration. A shell company, conduit, circular payment structure, or entity lacking decision-making capacity may lose treaty benefits and deductions and may face reassessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing sales, manipulating project completion percentages, issuing false invoices, understating VAT, fabricating expenses, or maintaining undeclared bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, late interest, 40% penalty for deliberate conduct, 80% penalty for fraudulent maneuvers or abusive concealment, and potential criminal tax fraud penalties of up to five years' imprisonment and EUR 500,000 fine; aggravated cases can reach seven years and EUR 3 million, subject to statutory conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may face criminal prosecution, personal fines, management bans, civil liability for intentional misconduct, and exceptional tax-liability proceedings where the director's fraudulent or seriously negligent conduct made recovery impossible. Corporate limited liability is not a defense to personal criminal conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: VAT carousel, false subcontracting, or fraudulent reverse charge
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming fictitious input VAT, using missing-trader chains, misclassifying construction subcontracting, or applying reverse charge without satisfying statutory conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT reassessment, recovery of improperly credited VAT, 40% or 80% penalties, late interest, possible joint-and-several recovery, and criminal sanctions for aggravated fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly authorize or facilitate fraudulent VAT arrangements may incur criminal liability, personal fines, professional disqualification, and civil recovery claims.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Overpriced foreign procurement, unsupported management fees, royalties for unused IP, interest on excessive related-party debt, non-arm's-length guarantees, or allocation of French project profit to a low-substance affiliate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment to arm's-length profit, withholding tax, denial of deductions, interest limitation consequences, penalties for inadequate documentation, and possible 40% or 80% penalties where deliberate evasion or abuse is established.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally exposed for fraudulent arrangements, inaccurate declarations, or deliberate destruction or concealment of supporting records; ordinary transfer-pricing reassessment does not automatically pierce limited liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing dividends, interest, or royalties through a conduit entity, using a nominal tax-resident recipient, back-to-back financing, or claiming treaty relief without beneficial ownership and substantive activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty relief, withholding tax at the domestic rate, interest, penalties, recovery from the payer in certain circumstances, and application of principal-purpose or abuse-of-law rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may face civil and criminal exposure if they knowingly certify false treaty documentation or organize fraudulent distributions; a travel ban is not an automatic tax sanction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, fictitious management, or permanent-establishment concealment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating French projects through an entity with no genuine decision-making, omitting a French fixed place of business or dependent-agent activity, or diverting contracts to an offshore company while French personnel execute the work.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: French corporate tax and VAT assessment, permanent-establishment attribution, withholding tax, penalties, interest, and possible abuse-of-law treatment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for deliberate concealment, fraudulent insolvency, or false accounting. French law does not automatically pierce the corporate veil solely because a company has limited substance, but courts may impose personal liability for separable personal misconduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining double books, backdating contracts, falsifying work certificates, creating fictitious suppliers, destroying accounting records, or concealing cash payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax penalties, rejection of accounts, statutory accounting sanctions, criminal charges for forgery, use of forged documents, fraud, or fraudulent bankruptcy, and possible prohibition from managing a business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability may include imprisonment and fines, together with management bans and civil restitution. Travel restrictions may be imposed only by a competent judicial authority and are not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained third-party payments, structuring payments to avoid controls, failing to identify beneficial owners, ignoring sanctions indicators, or processing suspicious letters of credit and wires.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reporting and control failures may lead to administrative, professional, and criminal consequences; laundering offenses can carry imprisonment and substantial fines, with enhanced sanctions for aggravated conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and employees may face individual criminal liability where they knowingly participate in laundering or deliberately obstruct required controls. Internal AML failures alone do not automatically create veil-piercing liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using sham subcontractors, misclassifying employees, omitting payroll, paying off-book labor, or failing to make required French social contributions on workers performing cleanroom fit-out activities in France.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Backdated social contributions, surcharges, labor-law penalties, loss of public contracts or subsidies, tax reassessment, and criminal sanctions for concealed work.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal criminal liability, management bans, and civil claims for intentional concealed work or serious breaches of payroll and worker-protection obligations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Construction, safety, and statutory insurance non-compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Performing regulated fit-out or construction work without required qualifications, professional liability insurance, ten-year construction insurance where applicable, worker-safety controls, or lawful subcontractor documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative orders, fines, work stoppage, civil damages, contract termination, exclusion from public procurement, and criminal liability for serious safety breaches.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur personal criminal exposure for deliberate safety violations or negligent homicide or injury, while civil liability may extend to uninsured or improperly supervised works.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misclassifying imported HVAC or cleanroom components, undervaluing goods, misdeclaring origin, bypassing sanctions, or supplying controlled technology to restricted counterparties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Customs duties, import VAT, seizure, administrative fines, loss of customs authorizations, sanctions enforcement, and criminal penalties depending on the breach.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible officers may face personal criminal sanctions for knowing customs fraud or sanctions evasion; asset freezes and travel restrictions may apply under sanctions or judicial measures but are not automatic consequences of ordinary customs errors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Transferring assets to group companies, preferring insiders, continuing to incur debts while insolvent, falsifying accounts, or stripping the SARL before a liquidation or restructuring.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Avoidance of transactions, repayment orders, liability for all or part of insolvency shortfall, bankruptcy-related penalties, management bans, and criminal sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may order contribution to insufficient assets and impose personal civil or criminal sanctions. This is a principal route through which limited liability can be displaced by director misconduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to preserve tax and commercial records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Inability to produce invoices, contracts, payroll files, transfer-pricing evidence, customs records, bank statements, project documentation, or electronic accounting trails during an audit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Rejection of accounting records, estimated assessment, reversal of deductions or VAT credits, documentation penalties, and increased penalties where concealment is inferred.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be sanctioned for intentional destruction, obstruction, or false responses. Ordinary record deficiencies generally create corporate tax liability rather than automatic personal liability.
